In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel multilayer beam-splitting technique for soft X-ray applications.
the fabrication of a self-standing Mo/Si multibeam splitter with high reflectivity, large and flat reflection area, high transmittance, and high damage resistance.
the development of a large and self-standing multilayer beam-splitter for soft x-ray applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a multilayer beam-splitter with a self-supporting active area can be fabricated by using a multilayer with a slightly tensile stress.
the beam splitters can be made large and flat, and can have a self-standing active area, if the multilayer stress is precisely controlled.

the multilayer stress can be precisely controlled by adjusting the multilayer deposition conditions to give a slightly compressive or tensile state and this enables the fabrication of large and flat reflection surfaces with a roughness of 1 nm (r. m. s.) or less, and also the removal of the supporting membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multilayer beam splitting is an efficient way to divide a beam of synchrotron X-ray radiation into two beams with equal intensity.
a large and flat beam splitter with a reflectivity of 27% (at 13.4-nm wavelength) can be realized by using a Mo/Si multlayer with a thickness of about 200 nm and a period of about 4.5 nm.
the Mo/Si multibeam splitter has been successfully demonstrated as a one-to- one beam splitter for a wide range of X-ray wavelengths.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the stress in the multilayers can be controlled to give a slightly tensioned state, enabling fabrication of a large, flat reflection surface, and making it possible to etching away the supporting membrane.
a self-standing Mo/Si multlalyer beam splitter can be fabricated with high reflectivity and high transmittance.
the beam splitter is a promising device for use in soft X-ray beamlines.
